title: Folding the Sheet: Folio, Quarto, Octavo
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Calculate the pages and sheets of paper in one copy of Virgil as a folio, a plain octavo, and an Aldine-style octavo, then explore any format, page density, and print run.

educational.topic: Folding the Sheet: Folio, Quarto, Octavo
learningObjectives: Calculate the number of pages and sheets of paper needed for one copy of Virgil's works in folio, quarto, or octavo format at a given number of lines per page, getting all three challenge calculations exactly right within two attempts each.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked practice problems with immediate feedback, then free exploration
keyQuestions: How many pages does one sheet make in each format?
Why must sheets per copy round up?
How much of the Aldine saving came from the fold, and how much from the denser page?
commonMisconceptions: A sheet is a page (a sheet makes 4, 8, or 16 pages).
The small format alone explains the Aldine savings; the compact type and missing commentary did not matter.
A cheaper book must hold a shorter text.
Pages divide evenly into sheets, so a part-sheet can be ignored.
assessmentOpportunities: Three challenge calculations, two attempts each (mastery: all three correct).
Follow-up: sheets for a quarto Virgil at 20 lines per page (81).
